investment_summary: NVIDIA's FY2026 10-K shows strong momentum: revenue rose 65% to $215.9 billion and free cash flow reached $96.7 billion [1]. Growth slowed from 114% in FY2025 and gross margin fell 3.9 points to 71.1% [1]. Consensus, dated after the 10-K, expects FY2027 revenue of $423.7 billion (+96%) and EPS of $9.67, with EPS estimates up about 7% over 90 days [3]. At an enterprise value of $3.69 trillion, the reverse DCF implies 26.2% annual revenue growth for ten years at a 15% WACC [2][3]. That is below the 100% three-year historical CAGR and far below near-term consensus, so the price assumes consensus is delivered and then a steep fade. Key risks are China export restrictions, a $4.5 billion H20 charge and 36% of revenue from two direct customers [1]. Net cash of $51.5 billion at year-end supports funding [2]. We see a high-quality franchise whose valuation hinges on Rubin shipments in the second half of fiscal 2027 [1].
key_takeaways: Growth should stay far ahead of peers into fiscal 2027 as Blackwell and networking ramp; Data Center revenue rose 68% [1].
Gross margin must recover from 71.1% to justify the premium, because the 3.9-point drop is the key test of pricing power [1].
The stock already prices in a sharp growth fade: the reverse DCF needs 26% ten-year growth while EPS estimates keep rising [2][3].
Free cash flow funds buybacks and a shrinking share count, but latest-quarter debt of $38.4 billion makes net cash a watch item [2].
business_overview:
NVIDIA, founded in 1993, is a data center scale AI infrastructure company that supplies GPUs, CPUs, networking, systems and the CUDA software platform for AI, gaming, professional visualization and automotive [1]. In fiscal 2026, which ended January 25, 2026, revenue rose 65% to $215.9 billion and net income rose 65% to $120.1 billion [1]. The company reports two segments: Compute & Networking, which contributed $193.5 billion, or about 90% of revenue, and Graphics, which contributed $22.5 billion [1].

Compute & Networking is the engine of the business. Data Center revenue rose 68%, compute revenue rose 59% on Blackwell demand, and networking revenue rose 142% on NVLink systems for GB200 and GB300 [1]. The 10-K cites more than 7.5 million developers using CUDA and GPUs and networking powering over 78% of the TOP500 supercomputers as the main sources of its advantage [1]. The filing gives no overall market share figure, so market position is judged from these indicators.

Graphics revenue rose 57% to $22.5 billion, with Professional Visualization up 70% on Blackwell and the DGX Spark launch, Gaming up 41% and Automotive up 39% [1]. Management expects supply constraints to weigh on Gaming from the first quarter of fiscal 2027. Strategic initiatives include Blackwell Ultra shipments from the second quarter of fiscal 2026, Rubin production shipments expected in the second half of fiscal 2027, and NVLink Fusion, which lets hyperscalers and custom ASIC designers integrate their own chips [1]. The company invested $17.5 billion in private companies and infrastructure funds, provided $3.5 billion of land, power and shell guarantees, and repurchased about $40 billion of stock [1]. An investment and partnership agreement with OpenAI is being finalized, but the filing gives no assurance it will be completed [1].
market_position:
NVIDIA's revenue is concentrated in the United States: customers headquartered outside the U.S. fell to 31% of fiscal 2026 revenue from 41%, and two direct customers accounted for 22% and 14% of revenue, or 36% combined (22% + 14%), mostly in Compute & Networking [1]. The filing does not name these customers. Some indirect customers are estimated to individually represent 10% or more of revenue [1].

China is the largest constraint on the franchise. The company states it was effectively foreclosed from China's data center compute market at fiscal year-end, earned about $60 million of H20 revenue under licenses against the $4.5 billion charge, and has generated no H200 revenue to date. Any H200 shipped to the U.S. would face a 25% tariff on importation [1]. China's antitrust regulators issued a preliminary finding on September 15, 2025 that NVIDIA's export-control compliance discriminated against China customers [1]. The 10-K names AMD, Intel, Broadcom and cloud providers designing their own chips as competitors [1].

No overall market share figure is given in the 10-K. For scale, competitors' FY2025 revenues were $34.6 billion for AMD, $63.9 billion for Broadcom and $52.9 billion for Intel, combined $151.4 billion. NVIDIA's $130.5 billion FY2025 revenue is about 86% of that combined figure [4]. Analyst consensus, dated after the 10-K, rates the stock Buy with an average target price of $244.71 (range $130 to $425) [3]. The stock closed at $192.40 with a 52-week range of $86.40 to $211.68 [2]. Consensus forward multiples in this report use a price of $144.31, so the price basis should be confirmed before any valuation decision [3].
operating_results:
Revenue rose 65% to $215.9 billion from $130.5 billion, with Compute & Networking up 67% and Graphics up 57% [1]. Gross profit grew about 57% to $153.5 billion, but gross margin fell 3.9 points to 71.1% from 75.0%, driven by the Hopper-to-Blackwell transition and a $4.5 billion H20 charge for excess inventory and purchase obligations [1]. Operating expenses rose 41% to $23.1 billion, slower than revenue, so operating margin eased only to 60.4% from 62.4% [1].

Net income grew 65% to $120.1 billion and diluted EPS rose 67% to $4.90 [1]. Other income of $9.0 billion, against $1.0 billion a year earlier, helped, while the effective tax rate rose to 15.1% from 13.3% [1]. Segment results show the margin pressure: Compute & Networking operating income rose 57% to $130.1 billion, but its margin fell to 67.3% from 71.3% because of the H20 charge. Graphics operating income rose 80% to $9.2 billion and its margin rose to 40.8% from 35.6% [1].

Cash generation remained strong. Operating cash flow rose to $102.7 billion from $64.1 billion, and free cash flow reached $96.7 billion against $60.9 billion [1][2]. Operating cash flow was $17.4 billion below net income because receivables absorbed $15.4 billion and inventory $11.3 billion [1]. Total assets rose 85% to $206.8 billion, with receivables of $38.5 billion, inventory of $21.4 billion and investments of $22.3 billion, and the current ratio fell to 3.9x from 4.4x [1]. Analysts' consensus of forward-looking EPS, dated after the 10-K, is covered in the valuation section [3].
risk_assessment:
The first risk is supply and demand mismatch. NVIDIA builds finished products and holds inventory ahead of anticipated demand, and the filing says it has previously experienced lead times of more than 12 months [1]. Non-cancellable purchase orders amplify the exposure, and the company has had to reduce prices, write down inventory, pay cancellation penalties and record impairments [1]. The filing says these risks grow as prepaids and purchase obligations become a larger portion of total supply, and that commitments have increased product costs [1].

The second risk is export controls and China. Licensing rules can change at any time, and the company may be unable to sell its inventory of restricted products [1]. The Chinese government has encouraged customers to purchase from China-based competitors and discouraged purchases of NVIDIA's data center products [1]. The $4.5 billion H20 charge set against roughly $60 million of licensed sales shows how little offset has been available. The preliminary antitrust finding could lead to financial penalties and restrictions on networking products, which would reach a segment that grew 142% [1].

The third risk is customer concentration and counterparty exposure. Two direct customers provided 36% of revenue, and most sales are on purchase orders that customers can cancel or delay with little notice and no penalty [1]. The company has granted extended payment terms, has been asked to provide financing, and has entered into long-term capacity purchase obligations and financial guarantees, including $3.5 billion of land, power and shell guarantees [1]. Insurance may not pay claims, and the OpenAI agreement is not assured [1]. Quality screens add context: the Piotroski F-Score is 4 of 9, the Altman Z-Score is 47.05 in the safe zone, and the Beneish M-Score of -1.13 sits above the -1.78 threshold, which is a statistical warning sign and not proof of manipulation [2]. Total debt was $11.0 billion at year-end but rose to $38.4 billion in the latest quarter, which is dated after the 10-K [2].
competitors_analysis:
The peers are AMD, Broadcom and Intel. AMD and Intel are named as competitors in the 10-K, and Broadcom is the closest business-model match among larger chip companies because it designs custom AI accelerators and data center networking [1]. Marvell has a similar model but is roughly 0.0x NVIDIA's size, so it was not used. On size, the peer screen shows revenue of $45.4 billion for AMD, $89.1 billion for Broadcom and $59.9 billion for Intel, each 0.1x to 0.2x NVIDIA's revenue in that screen [4].

On FY2025 financials, NVIDIA's gross margin of 75.0% is well above Broadcom's 67.8%, AMD's 49.5% and Intel's 34.8%, and its EBITDA margin of 66.0% compares with 54.3%, 21.0% and 27.2% [4]. NVIDIA's revenue growth of 114% compares with 34.3% for AMD, 23.9% for Broadcom and -0.5% for Intel [4]. Its return on invested capital of 83.3% is far above Broadcom's 13.2%, AMD's 4.8% and Intel's 1.2%, and free cash flow of $60.9 billion is about 2.3 times Broadcom's $26.9 billion and about nine times AMD's $6.7 billion; Intel's free cash flow was negative at -$4.9 billion [4].

Valuation is more balanced. NVIDIA's EV/EBITDA was 34.1x in FY2025, below AMD's 47.8x and Broadcom's 51.9x, and above Intel's 15.1x; it fell to 32.1x in FY2026 [4]. On consensus, NVIDIA's forward P/E is 14.9x for FY2027 and 8.7x for FY2028 [3]. The reported FCF conversion of 0.81 in FY2026 is below AMD's and Broadcom's reported figures, but the definitions differ and should be checked before comparison [4]. The peer comparison supports a premium to Intel and a multiple comparable to AMD and Broadcom, while the main threat is custom silicon from cloud providers and competitors that could erode NVIDIA's margins [1].

investment_theses.thesis: Data center demand keeps NVIDIA's growth well above peers through fiscal 2027.
investment_theses.evidence: Data Center revenue rose 68% and networking rose 142% in FY2026 [1]; FY2027 consensus revenue is $423.7 billion, up 96% [3].
investment_theses.signpost: Data Center revenue growth above 50% year over year in each FY2027 quarter reported, and Rubin production shipments starting in the second half of FY2027 [1][3].
investment_theses.invalidation: Data Center growth below 25% year over year in any FY2027 quarter, or FY2027 revenue more than 10% below the $423.7 billion consensus [3].

investment_theses.thesis: Gross margin recovers above 72% as Blackwell yields mature and the H20 charge does not recur.
investment_theses.evidence: Gross margin fell to 71.1% from 75.0% because of the Hopper-to-Blackwell transition and the $4.5 billion H20 charge [1]; Broadcom's FY2025 gross margin was 67.8% [4].
investment_theses.signpost: Quarterly gross margin back above 72% by the end of FY2027 (January 2027) [1].
investment_theses.invalidation: Gross margin below 70% in any FY2027 quarter, or new inventory provisions or purchase-obligation charges [1].

investment_theses.thesis: The stock is priced for a steep growth fade, so returns depend on consensus EPS being delivered.
investment_theses.evidence: The reverse DCF implies 26.2% growth for ten years at a 15% WACC [2][3]; the forward P/E is 14.9x for FY2027 and 8.7x for FY2028, and FY2028 EPS estimates rose 27.7% over 90 days [3].
investment_theses.signpost: FY2027 EPS at or above the $9.67 consensus, and the FY2028 EPS estimate holding above $16 through the FY2027 year-end [3].
investment_theses.invalidation: FY2027 EPS consensus falls below the $9.05 level from 90 days earlier, or the reverse DCF growth requirement rises above 30% [2][3].

investment_theses.thesis: Free cash flow and net cash can absorb the China and customer shocks without strain.
investment_theses.evidence: Free cash flow of $96.7 billion and net cash of $51.5 billion at year-end [1][2]; two direct customers provide 36% of revenue and China is effectively closed [1].
investment_theses.signpost: Net cash stays positive in each FY2027 quarter, and any H200 revenue is disclosed in the first half of FY2027 [1][2].
investment_theses.invalidation: Net cash turns negative, or a China antitrust penalty or networking restriction is imposed [1][2].
